1: # Video kit: recording, assembly, and self test for the 2 minute demo
2: 
3: The Sheridan Datathon 2026 submission needs a demo video of at most 120
4: seconds (mandatory in 2026, see docs/research.md). This directory holds the
5: two shell tools that produce it plus a synthetic self test. Everything here is
6: shell plus ffmpeg: no Python, no uv environment, no npm scripts.
7: 
8: | File | Purpose |
9: |------|---------|
10: | `record.sh` | capture one screen clip with ffmpeg avfoundation (macOS) |
11: | `assemble.sh` | concat clips, optionally burn an .srt, enforce the 120s hard cap, emit a YouTube ready MP4 |
12: | `test_assemble.sh` | synthetic end to end test of `assemble.sh` (color clips, no footage) |
13: | `../video/` (docs) | timed shot script and the capture plan: `docs/video/script.md`, `docs/video/plan.md` |
14: 
15: ## Tool requirements
16: 
17: | Tool | Verified version on this machine | Check |
18: |------|----------------------------------|-------|
19: | bash | 3.2.57 (macOS default, scripts avoid bash 4 features) | `bash --version` |
20: | ffmpeg | 9.0.2 (Homebrew `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/ffmpeg/9.0.2_1`, Apple clang 21.0.0) | `ffmpeg -version` |
21: | ffprobe | 9.0.2 (ships with ffmpeg, used for every duration check) | `ffprobe -version` |
22: | avfoundation | built into this ffmpeg (macOS screen capture input) | `./scripts/video/record.sh --list-devices` |
23: 
24: Verified `ffmpeg -version` header on this machine:
25: 
26: ```
27: ffmpeg version 9.0.2 Copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers
28: built with Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2)
29: ```
30: 
31: The build configuration includes `--enable-libx264` and
32: `--enable-videotoolbox` (recording and encoding are covered) but does NOT
33: include `--enable-libass`, so the `subtitles` filter is missing here. See
34: "Burning subtitles" below.
35: 
36: ## Quick start
37: 
38: ```bash
39: # 0. one time checks
40: ffmpeg -version
41: ./scripts/video/record.sh --list-devices
42: ./scripts/video/test_assemble.sh
43: 
44: # 1. build and serve the app the judges will see
45: npm run build
46: npm run preview            # http://localhost:4173
47: 
48: # 2. record each shot (full list and durations in docs/video/plan.md)
49: ./scripts/video/record.sh -d 14 -o scripts/video/captures/clip_01_question.mp4
50: ./scripts/video/record.sh -d 28 -o scripts/video/captures/clip_02_f1_f2.mp4
51: 
52: # 3. assemble in shot order (the hard 120s check runs before encoding)
53: ./scripts/video/assemble.sh -o scripts/video/final/demo.mp4 \
54:     scripts/video/captures/clip_01_question.mp4 \
55:     scripts/video/captures/clip_02_f1_f2.mp4
56: # clip list order must match the shot order in docs/video/script.md
57: 
58: # 4. verify what you would upload
59: ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1 \
60:     scripts/video/final/demo.mp4
61: ```
62: 
63: ## record.sh
64: 
65: Records the whole screen (or `--device N` for a second screen) to H.264 MP4
66: at 30 fps, silent by default (`--mic` adds the first microphone).
67: 
68: ```bash
69: ./scripts/video/record.sh --help
70: ./scripts/video/record.sh --list-devices
71: ./scripts/video/record.sh -d 24 --mic -o scripts/video/captures/clip_04_game_auto.mp4
72: ./scripts/video/record.sh -d 9 -i 5 -o scripts/video/captures/clip_07_second_screen.mp4
73: ```
74: 
75: Practical notes:
76: 
77: * Capture the built app, not the dev server: `npm run build && npm run preview`
78:   then open `http://localhost:4173`. The judges run the same static build.
79: * macOS requires Screen Recording permission for your terminal the first time
80:   (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording), otherwise the
81:   capture is black.
82: * Minimize the terminal or shoot a second screen so tooling never appears.
83: * Keep fps, size, and duration settings consistent across clips of one video
84:   so `assemble.sh` can concat them.
85: 
86: ## assemble.sh
87: 
88: Concatenates with the ffmpeg concat demuxer, then performs one re-encode.
89: 
90: ```bash
91: ./scripts/video/assemble.sh --help
92: 
93: # normal case, under the cap
94: ./scripts/video/assemble.sh -o scripts/video/final/demo.mp4 \
95:     scripts/video/captures/clip_01.mp4 scripts/video/captures/clip_02.mp4
96: 
97: # burn captions (needs a libass build, see below)
98: ./scripts/video/assemble.sh -o scripts/video/final/demo.mp4 \
99:     --subtitles scripts/video/captions.srt scripts/video/captures/*.mp4
100: 
101: # overlong input: refused by default (exit 4)
102: ./scripts/video/assemble.sh -o scripts/video/final/demo.mp4 scripts/video/captures/*.mp4
103: #   ERROR: clip list totals 134.500s, which is 14.500s OVER the 120s hard maximum.
104: 
105: # only an explicit operator flag may cut at exactly 120s
106: ./scripts/video/assemble.sh -o scripts/video/final/demo.mp4 \
107:     --allow-trim scripts/video/captures/*.mp4
108: ```
109: 
110: Guarantees:
111: 
112: * upfront `ffprobe` duration sum, loud refusal over 120s, exit code 4,
113:   no output file written,
114: * `--allow-trim` is the only way to get a cut at 120s, and it prints a warning,
115: * resolution mismatch between clips fails loudly before encoding,
116: * output is H.264 (libx264), yuv420p, `+faststart`, AAC audio when the clip
117:   set has audio (`-an` keeps silent clip sets clean, no unused-option noise),
118:   and an audio presence mismatch between clips warns before encoding,
119: * the finished file is re-probed: over 120.5s or wrong codec/pix_fmt exits 5.
120: 
121: Exit codes: `2` usage or input error, `3` subtitles unavailable, `4` over the
122: hard maximum without `--allow-trim`, `5` output verification failed.
123: 
124: ## Burning subtitles
125: 
126: `--subtitles file.srt` burns captions with this forced style (readable at
127: phone size): Helvetica 22, white with a black 2px outline, bottom center,
128: 26px bottom margin.
129: 
130: The current Homebrew ffmpeg 9.0.2 on this machine has no `subtitles` filter
131: (no libass), so the script detects that up front and exits 3 with instructions
132: instead of failing mid encode. Ways to get a capable build:
133: 
134: ```bash
135: sudo port install ffmpeg                     # MacPorts, libass enabled
136: # or a static arm64 build: https://ffmpeg.martin-riedl.de/
137: # 'brew reinstall ffmpeg' does not help: the Homebrew formula here has no libass
138: # (verify with: brew deps ffmpeg)
139: ```
140: 
141: Fallback with zero extra tooling: assemble without `--subtitles` (all key
142: numbers are already on screen as text cards) and upload the same `.srt` as
143: YouTube captions, which the upload checklist in `docs/video/plan.md`
144: covers.
145: 
146: Known gap: `assemble.sh` does not mix a separate narration track. Per
147: docs/decisions.md the interim plan is pre-generated narration, so if voice-over
148: is used, mux it in an editor after assembly or extend this script.
149: 
150: ## Self test
151: 
152: ```bash
153: ./scripts/video/test_assemble.sh
154: ```
155: 
156: It generates three 5s color clips, assembles them (expects about 15s,
157: h264/yuv420p), then builds a 150s input and asserts that `assemble.sh`
158: refuses it without `--allow-trim` (exit 4, message, no output file) and cuts
159: it to at most 120s with the flag. Exit code 0 means all assertions passed.
160: 
161: Syntax check both scripts at any time:
162: 
163: ```bash
164: bash -n scripts/video/record.sh scripts/video/assemble.sh scripts/video/test_assemble.sh
165: ```
166: 
167: ## Conventions in this directory
168: 
169: * 4 space indent in shell bodies where indented, K&R style case/if braces,
170:   `snake_case` functions, `SCREAMING_SNAKE` for the `MAX_SECONDS` constant.
171: * No em dashes, double hyphens, or dash equivalents in prose (shell flags such
172:   as `--allow-trim` are fine).
173: * Captured media lands in `captures/` and `final/`, both git ignored; nothing
174:   in this directory should be committed by hand.

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: #
3: # record.sh: capture one screen clip for the Ledger Odyssey demo video.
4: #
5: # Uses ffmpeg's avfoundation input (macOS only) to record the screen into an
6: # H.264 MP4 that assemble.sh can concat later. Pure shell plus ffmpeg: no
7: # Python, no uv environment.
8: #
9: # Capturing the built app (preferred over the dev server, judges see the
10: # same code that ships):
11: #     npm run build
12: #     npm run preview                 # serves dist/ at http://localhost:4173
13: #     open http://localhost:4173      # hide the bookmarks bar, pick a zoom
14: # Then minimize this terminal (or record a second screen with --device)
15: # before you start recording, so the terminal never appears in the shot.
16: #
17: # First run on a new Mac: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen
18: # Recording must allow your terminal app, otherwise ffmpeg captures black.
19: #
20: # Examples:
21: #     ./scripts/video/record.sh --list-devices
22: #     ./scripts/video/record.sh -d 14 -o scripts/video/captures/clip_01_question.mp4
23: #     ./scripts/video/record.sh -d 24 --mic -o scripts/video/captures/clip_04_game.mp4
24: #     ./scripts/video/record.sh -d 9 -i 5 -o scripts/video/captures/clip_07_second_screen.mp4
25: 
26: set -euo pipefail
27: 
28: SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
29: 
30: # Defaults, all overridable from the command line.
31: DURATION=30           # seconds, match the shot budget in docs/video/script.md
32: FPS=30                # keep every clip at 30 fps so concat stays smooth
33: OUTPUT=""             # empty means captures/clip_<timestamp>.mp4
34: SCREEN_DEVICE=""      # empty means auto-detect "Capture screen 0"
35: AUDIO_DEVICE="none"   # "none" is silent, --mic flips it to the first microphone
36: SIZE=""               # optional scale, for example 1600x900
37: 
38: usage() {
39:     cat <<'EOF'
40: Usage: record.sh [options]
41: 
42:   -d, --duration SECONDS   how long to record (default 30)
43:   -o, --output PATH        where to write the clip
44:                            (default captures/clip_<timestamp>.mp4 next to this script)
45:   -f, --fps N              capture frame rate (default 30)
46:   -i, --device INDEX       avfoundation video device index (default: auto-detect)
47:       --mic                also record the first microphone (silent by default)
48:       --size WxH           scale the recording, for example 1600x900
49:       --list-devices       print the avfoundation device list and exit
50:   -h, --help               show this help
51: 
52: Notes:
53:   * Build and preview the app first: npm run build && npm run preview
54:   * macOS asks for Screen Recording permission the first time
55:     (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording).
56:   * Keep duration, fps, and size identical across the clips of one video so
57:     assemble.sh can concat them without surprises.
58: EOF
59: }
60: 
61: need_value() {
62:     # Called as: need_value "$@" right after matching a flag that takes one.
63:     if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then
64:         echo "ERROR: $1 expects a value" >&2
65:         exit 2
66:     fi
67: }
68: 
69: list_devices() {
70:     # ffmpeg exits non-zero after printing the device list, hence the guard.
71:     ffmpeg -hide_banner -f avfoundation -list_devices true -i "" 2>&1 || true
72: }
73: 
74: detect_screen_device() {
75:     # Matches a line like: [AVFoundation indev @ 0x...] [4] Capture screen 0
76:     list_devices | sed -n 's/.*\] \[\([0-9][0-9]*\)\] Capture screen 0.*/\1/p' | head -n 1
77: }
78: 
79: detect_first_microphone() {
80:     # First entry under the "AVFoundation audio devices" header.
81:     list_devices | sed -n '/AVFoundation audio devices:/,$s/.*\] \[\([0-9][0-9]*\)\] .*/\1/p' | head -n 1
82: }
83: 
84: while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
85:     case "$1" in
86:         -d|--duration) need_value "$@"; DURATION="$2"; shift 2 ;;
87:         -o|--output) need_value "$@"; OUTPUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
88:         -f|--fps) need_value "$@"; FPS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
89:         -i|--device) need_value "$@"; SCREEN_DEVICE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
90:         --mic) AUDIO_DEVICE="auto"; shift ;;
91:         --size) need_value "$@"; SIZE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
92:         --list-devices) list_devices; exit 0 ;;
93:         -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
94:         *) echo "ERROR: unknown argument '$1'" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
95:     esac
96: done
97: 
98: command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: ffmpeg not found on PATH" >&2; exit 2; }
99: command -v ffprobe >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: ffprobe not found on PATH" >&2; exit 2; }
100: 
101: # Strict number shape: digits with at most one dot. The old character
102: # class accepted "1..2" and "30.", which ffmpeg then rejects raw.
103: if ! [[ "$DURATION" =~ ^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
104:     echo "ERROR: --duration must be seconds as digits with at most one dot (for example 30 or 12.5), got '$DURATION'" >&2
105:     exit 2
106: fi
107: case "$FPS" in
108:     ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "ERROR: --fps must be a whole number, got '$FPS'" >&2; exit 2 ;;
109: esac
110: case "$SIZE" in
111:     '') ;;
112:     *[!0-9x]*) echo "ERROR: --size must look like 1600x900, got '$SIZE'" >&2; exit 2 ;;
113: esac
114: 
115: if [ -z "$OUTPUT" ]; then
116:     OUTPUT="$SCRIPT_DIR/captures/clip_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).mp4"
117: fi
118: mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUTPUT")"
119: 
120: if [ -z "$SCREEN_DEVICE" ]; then
121:     SCREEN_DEVICE="$(detect_screen_device || true)"
122: fi
123: if [ -z "$SCREEN_DEVICE" ]; then
124:     SCREEN_DEVICE=4
125:     echo "note: could not auto-detect 'Capture screen 0', falling back to device 4 (run --list-devices to check)" >&2
126: fi
127: 
128: if [ "$AUDIO_DEVICE" = "auto" ]; then
129:     AUDIO_DEVICE="$(detect_first_microphone || true)"
130:     if [ -z "$AUDIO_DEVICE" ]; then
131:         echo "ERROR: no microphone found, drop --mic or pass a device with --list-devices" >&2
132:         exit 2
133:     fi
134: fi
135: 
136: echo "Recording ${DURATION}s from video device ${SCREEN_DEVICE}, audio device ${AUDIO_DEVICE}, ${FPS} fps ..."
137: 
138: cmd=(ffmpeg -hide_banner -y
139:     -f avfoundation -framerate "$FPS" -capture_cursor 1
140:     -i "${SCREEN_DEVICE}:${AUDIO_DEVICE}"
141:     -t "$DURATION"
142:     -c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p)
143: 
144: if [ "$AUDIO_DEVICE" != "none" ]; then
145:     cmd+=(-c:a aac -b:a 128k)
146: fi
147: if [ -n "$SIZE" ]; then
148:     cmd+=(-vf "scale=${SIZE}")
149: fi
150: cmd+=(-movflags +faststart "$OUTPUT")
151: 
152: "${cmd[@]}"
153: 
154: actual="$(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1 "$OUTPUT")"
155: echo "Done: ${OUTPUT} (${actual}s)."
156: echo "Next: check it with 'ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1 \"$OUTPUT\"' and list it first in assemble.sh."

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: #
3: # assemble.sh: concat recorded clips into the final demo MP4.
4: #
5: # What it does, in order:
6: #   1. reads the clip list in the order given (ffmpeg concat demuxer),
7: #   2. measures every clip with ffprobe and sums the durations,
8: #   3. refuses to encode anything when the total is over the HARD 120 second
9: #      maximum (Sheridan Datathon 2026 mandatory demo video), unless the
10: #      operator passes --allow-trim to cut the result at exactly 120s,
11: #   4. optionally burns an .srt caption file with a readable forced style,
12: #   5. encodes one MP4: H.264 (libx264), yuv420p, +faststart, AAC audio if
13: #      any clip carries audio. That is the combination YouTube accepts
14: #      without re-encoding complaints,
15: #   6. re-probes the result and fails loudly if it exceeds 120s plus the
16: #      0.5s AAC frame padding slack (120.5s), or if the codec is wrong.
17: #
18: # The 120s input maximum is hard. The post-encode re-probe is the only
19: # place with slack: AAC frame padding can read a cut of exactly 120s as
20: # 120.2s, so the verify limit is 120.5s (MAX_SECONDS plus SLACK_SECONDS)
21: # and nothing beyond it.
22: #
23: # Options must come before the clip list.
24: #
25: # Examples:
26: #   ./scripts/video/assemble.sh -o scripts/video/final/demo.mp4 \
27: #       scripts/video/captures/clip_01_question.mp4 \
28: #       scripts/video/captures/clip_02_f1_f2.mp4
29: #
30: #   ./scripts/video/assemble.sh -o final.mp4 --subtitles captions.srt clip_01.mp4 clip_02.mp4
31: #
32: #   ./scripts/video/assemble.sh -o final.mp4 --allow-trim clip_01.mp4 clip_02.mp4
33: #
34: # Exit codes: 2 input or usage error, 3 subtitles unavailable in this ffmpeg
35: # build, 4 over the 120s maximum without --allow-trim, 5 output verification
36: # failed.
37: 
38: set -euo pipefail
39: 
40: MAX_SECONDS=120

57:   -h, --help             show this help
58: 
59: Rules:
60:   * Clips play in the order given and must share resolution and frame rate.
61:   * The summed clip duration must be at most 120 seconds. The check runs
62:     BEFORE any encoding; an overlong list exits with code 4 and no output.

10: ## Purpose and audience
11: 
12: * Purpose: win Best Data Visualization and Storytelling through the population
13:   finding plus the live shock, and support the Tangerine sponsor track with a
14:   live run of the exact judge definitions.
15: * Primary audience: judges scanning the entry in about five minutes of attention.
16: * Secondary audience: Devpost reviewers checking that the shipped claims match
17:   the video.
18: * Success: a viewer can repeat the one line pitch (one percent of accounts hold
19:   under three months of runway at baseline, ten percent under a layoff twist)
20:   and remembers the verdict falling to 1.5 months with the pin matching it.
21: 
22: ## Ranked format concepts
23: 
24: * Option 1, chosen: full screen recording of the built app, six clips, voice
25:   over recorded with each clip, no camera.
26:   * Pros: fastest to retake per scene, the interface is the product, the sticky
27:     judge bar and every honesty label stay legible at 1080p.
28:   * Cons: no human face, so the narration has to carry the trust.
29: * Option 2: face cam in the corner plus screen recording.
30:   * Pros: human connection.
31:   * Cons: the keycaps, guard chips, and provenance line are small; a corner cam
32:     covers the judge bar, which is a required frame.
33: * Option 3: one continuous 120 second take with live narration.
34:   * Pros: no edit, perfect pacing.
35:   * Cons: one flub anywhere forces a full re record; the brief asks for one to
36:     two retakes per scene, which only works in pieces.
37: 
38: ## Style guide
39: 
40: * Palette: the app's own dark console tokens, so nothing in the edit competes
41:   with the band colors (critical, storm warning, watch, fair skies, clear).
42: * Type: no burned in typography except the app's own. Any editor overlay (lower
43:   third, end card) uses monospace to match the header, and carries no em dash,
44:   en dash, minus sign, double hyphen, or spaced hyphen, per `src/dashScan.test.ts`.
45: * Captions: export an SRT from the edit and upload it as YouTube captions. The
46:   local Homebrew ffmpeg has no libass, so `assemble.sh --subtitles` exits 3
47:   (see `scripts/video/README.md`); do not burn captions.
48: * Music: none, or a bed at minus 24 dB under the voice. The narration must stay
49:   intelligible on a laptop speaker.
50: * Pacing: hold every headline at least 2 seconds, let the forecast strip finish
51:   its roughly 1 second tile animation before moving, and never cut while a
52:   number is still changing.
53: 
54: ## Stand out strategy
55: 
56: * First 5 seconds: the atlas headline alone, no title card, no logo animation.
57:   The first spoken words are the finding.
58: * Gifable moment: the `1` keypress that moves the headline from 1% to 10% with
59:   `At baseline: 1% (60 of 4,500)` staying printed underneath.
